title: How JavaScript runs code
idea: JavaScript runs your code in two passes: first it sets up memory for every variable and function, then it executes line by line using a call stack.

analogy.text: A chef first lays out every ingredient on the counter, then cooks step by step. A sub-recipe puts a new card on top of the pile.
analogy.breaks: Real stacks hold one function call per card, and cards are tiny and fast.

points: Creation phase: variables and functions are registered before any line runs.
Execution phase: lines run in order, one at a time.
Calling a function pushes a new frame on the call stack.
Returning pops the frame and resumes the caller.

hero.title: The call stack, step by step

steps.caption: Creation phase: JavaScript registers price, double and result before running anything.
Line 1 runs: price is initialised to 10.
Line 5 calls double(price). JavaScript pauses here and pushes a new frame.
Inside the new frame, n * 2 gives 20, ready to return.
double returns 20 and its frame is popped. result receives 20.
Line 6 prints 20. The stack holds only Global again: the program is done.

code.caption: Run it, then add a fourth function and predict the order before you press Run.

code.title: Hoisting
code.caption: Functions are ready early. var exists but is empty. let sits in a dead zone.

pitfalls: `let` and `const` exist before their line, but reading them early throws a ReferenceError.
Infinite recursion keeps pushing frames until the stack overflows with a RangeError.

quiz.why: `var a` is registered in the creation phase as undefined. The `= 5` only runs on line 2.

takeaway: Memory first, then execution; every call is a frame on the stack.
